prompt.brief: Design an LLM inference platform that serves multiple model variants with streaming output, continuous batching, KV-cache management, GPU isolation, quotas, and safe rollout and fallback.
successSignals: Separate model and tokenizer artifacts, deployment policy, request queues, GPU workers, KV caches, and usage accounting.
Route by model, context length, priority, and tenant while using continuous batching without allowing long prompts to starve short requests.
Stream tokens with cancellation and backpressure, enforce prompt/output limits, and preserve the last healthy model during rollout.
Explain quantization, autoscaling, cache eviction, multi-region routing, safety, privacy, and cost attribution.

functional: Register model versions, deploy GPU pools, submit chat or completion requests, stream tokens, cancel requests, and retrieve usage.
Support model routing, prompt templates, safety policy, tenant quotas, priority, batch inference, and deployment health.
Expose time to first token, inter-token latency, queue time, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, errors, and model version.
nonFunctional: Target p95 time to first token below 500 ms and bound output streaming latency for interactive requests.
Handle 100,000 concurrent requests through model-specific queues and GPU pools with admission control.
Make request accounting, cancellation, retries, and billing idempotent; do not duplicate external tool effects.
Route to a smaller or cached model and preserve active streams when a model pool is degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Serve 100,000 concurrent requests, 10,000 tokens per second per pool, and dozens of model variants.
Partition by model, region, tenant, and prompt-size class; isolate long-context and batch workloads.
Retain signed model manifests, request metadata, safety decisions, and usage records while bounding KV caches.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the LLM inference platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional LLM inference platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return LLM inference platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition LLM inference platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound LLM inference platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for LLM inference platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable LLM inference platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable LLM inference platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure LLM inference platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
